mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 shows negative returns, or correlation is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 10% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment exceeds 10% but S&P 500 returns are non-negative, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 220, inflationary pressures may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Both conditions met but S&P 500 returns are positive, or no significant correlation.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO) growth during an expansion signals increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the relationship is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below $350,000 million indicates reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales fall below threshold but S&P 500 returns are non-negative, or the correlation is insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) remains high, it may indicate imbalanced economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Both conditions met but S&P 500 returns are positive, or no significant correlation.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are non-negative, or the effect is not statistically significant.
